title_he: לֹא אֶשְׁכַּח יוֹם אֲדֹנִי אֵצֶל הַצְּלָב

lines: לֹא אֶשְׁכַּח יוֹם אֲדֹנִי אֵצֶל הַצְּלָב
הֵן יוֹם יָבוֹא אֲדֹנִי כִּי תָשׁוּב

review: The Arabic prints the third and fourth lines of each stanza in parentheses (a refrain within the stanza) and closes every stanza with يا سيدي; Hebrew keeps both conventions, including the parentheses, so the printed layout matches.
1:2 הִגְלֵיתָ לִי אַהֲבָתְךָ — 'You revealed Your love to me'; גִּלָּה is the biblical verb of uncovering (Amos 3:7), and the Arabic أَعْلَنْتَ is the same idea.
3:1 אֲדֹן הַדֶּרֶךְ — 'Lord of the way', for رَبُّ الْهُدَى; the construct with the definite noun is used instead of a noun of guidance, which Hebrew lacks in the right register.
3:2 הַטּוֹב וְהַחֶסֶד — Psalm 23:6 (אַךְ טוֹב וָחֶסֶד יִרְדְּפוּנִי), quoted because the Arabic الْخَيْرُ وَالرَّحْمَةُ is that verse.
4:3 אָמֵן אֲדֹנִי בּוֹאָה — Revelation 22:20 (אָמֵן, בֹּאָה אֲדֹנֵינוּ); the stanza ends the hymn on the church's own prayer.
